planting.note: Plant divisions in fall or early spring in part shade to shade with fertile, well-drained soil; Charmer is a vigorous Frostkiss hybrid grown for oversized flowers as much as its marbled foliage.

directions: Charmer is a Frostkiss-series hybrid (Rodney Davey Marbled Group) crossing H. x hybridus lines with silver-marbled foliage parentage to produce unusually large single blooms. Flowers open dark pink and age to a stippled, burgundy-flecked finish, held above dark green leaves patterned with silvery marbling that stays attractive through the seasons. Bloom begins in mid-winter and continues into mid-spring, making this a long-season performer for the shaded border. Divide clumps only when crowded, as this hybrid resents frequent disturbance.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall or early spring in part shade with fertile, well-drained soil; Vibey Velvet pairs deep-toned flowers with silvery marbled foliage for year-round interest.

directions: A newer entry in the Frostkiss series of marbled-leaf hellebore hybrids, Vibey Velvet carries generously sized, deep reddish-purple flowers that hover on sturdy stems above a mound of silvery-green, net-veined evergreen foliage. The flowers hold their rich color well as they age rather than fading quickly, and bloom spans the winter-into-spring window typical of the series. Its compact habit suits smaller shade borders or containers better than larger-growing hellebore types. Keep soil consistently moist but never waterlogged, especially while plants establish.

scientific_name: Helleborus x nigercors 'HGC Ice Breaker Bonny'

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade.

directions: Bonny is a Gold Collection selection in the Ice Breaker line of sterile H. niger x H. argutifolius hybrids, chosen for large, rounded cream flowers edged in a rose-pink picotee that face outward above the foliage. Glossy, silvery-green, spiny-margined evergreen leaves inherited from its Corsican parent let it tolerate more direct sun than typical Lenten roses. As an interspecific sterile hybrid it never sets seed, so clumps increase only slowly and are best left undisturbed once established. Bloom runs from winter into spring, extending the garden's color well ahead of most perennials.

scientific_name: Helleborus x nigercors 'HGC Ice Breaker Ruby'

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade.

directions: Ruby is the deep red-flowered member of the sterile Ice Breaker hybrid group, descended from crosses between H. niger and H. argutifolius. Its richly colored, outward-facing blooms contrast with glossy, leathery evergreen foliage that carries a hint of its Corsican parent's spiny edge, and the sun tolerance of that parentage makes it easier to place than many Lenten roses. Flowering begins in winter and carries on into spring, giving reliable color during the slowest season in a shaded or partly sunny bed. Because it is sterile, increase the planting by division of established clumps rather than by seed.

common_name: Pink Promise Hellebore (Gold Collection Ice N' Roses Series)
scientific_name: Helleborus x glandorfensis 'HGC Ice N' Roses Pink Promise'

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in fall or early spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in dappled sun to partial shade.

directions: Pink Promise belongs to the Gold Collection's Ice N' Roses line, bred for a long winter-into-spring bloom season on compact, well-branched plants. Its light pink, forward-facing flowers are finely freckled with red dots and trail lighter streaks toward the center, each centered on a prominent boss of stamens. Leathery, dark evergreen foliage forms a tidy mound that stays presentable through all four seasons, building width faster than height as the clump matures. Grow in consistently moist, fertile soil, and avoid moving established plants since hellebores resent root disturbance.

common_name: Early Rose Hellebore (Gold Collection Ice N' Roses Series)
scientific_name: Helleborus x glandorfensis 'HGC Ice N' Roses Early Rose'

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in fall in humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Early Rose begins flowering well before most Lenten roses.

directions: True to its name, Early Rose opens its large, rounded, light rose-pink flowers starting in late autumn, well ahead of the main late-winter flush most Ice N' Roses siblings produce. Blooms face outward to upward above a vigorous mound of dark, leathery, palmate evergreen leaves, and the plant is noted for long-lived, robust growth that broadens steadily over the years. It tolerates more direct sun than many hybrid hellebores, making it useful in a wider range of garden positions. Feed lightly in spring and keep soil evenly moist for the best repeat bloom the following season.

common_name: Early Red Hellebore (Gold Collection Ice N' Roses Series)
scientific_name: Helleborus x glandorfensis 'HGC Ice N' Roses Early Red'

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in fall in moist, fertile, well-drained, neutral-to-alkaline soil in full sun to partial shade.

directions: Early Red stands out in the Ice N' Roses line for its exceptionally early bloom window, opening deep plum-purple to dark red flowers as early as November and continuing into March. The color holds well as flowers age instead of fading to the washed-out tones common in many hellebores, giving a longer effective display. Clump-forming evergreen to semi-evergreen foliage provides a neat backdrop through the colder months before the next flush of leaves emerges in spring. Give it fertile, consistently moist soil on the neutral-to-alkaline side for the strongest flowering performance.
